Fit Independent Posteriors per Block

Source: R/compute_posterior.R
fit_block_posterior.Rd

Splits data according to partition, then calls the unchanged posterior_mean/optim_hp pipeline independently per sub-problem (per block, or per (Group, block) when pooled = FALSE), collecting the results into a list consultable via get_sigmak_block/get_muk_block. No result fusion happens here – each sub-problem stays a genuine bayesomics_posterior object, so no numeric primitive is reimplemented.

Passing partition = partition_dense() (or, equivalently, NULL) collapses this to a single sub-problem covering the whole dataset – with the same pooled default as posterior_mean() (TRUE), this reproduces posterior_mean(data) exactly, so calling fit_block_posterior() with nothing else specified stays agnostic to the non-partitioned baseline.

Usage

fit_block_posterior(
  data,
  partition,
  kern = NULL,
  pooled = TRUE,
  mu_0 = 1,
  lambda_0 = 1,
  obs_noise = 0,
  df_warn = 8,
  prior_mean = 0,
  prior_cov = 1,
  pen_diag = 1e-06
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, same requirements as posterior_mean.

partition

A partition_strategy object (e.g. partition_by_id, partition_by_range, partition_from_annotation, partition_diagonal), or NULL / partition_dense() for a single block.

kern

NULL (closed form, as in posterior_mean()), or an UNFITTED kernel object (template) – in that case optim_hp() is called once per sub-problem before building its posterior (mirroring how posterior_mean() never fits kern itself when it is supplied, see R/optim_kernel.R).

pooled

A single parameter threaded to both branches: when kern = NULL, passed straight through to posterior_mean(kern = NULL, pooled = pooled); when kern is an unfitted template, TRUE fits one optim_hp(group_col = "Group") shared across every Group within a block, FALSE fits an independent optim_hp() per (Group, block). Defaults to TRUE, matching posterior_mean()'s own default.

mu_0, lambda_0, obs_noise, df_warn

Forwarded to posterior_mean() on every sub-problem; see its documentation.

prior_mean, prior_cov, pen_diag

Forwarded to optim_hp() when kern is an unfitted template; see its documentation.

Value

A block_posterior_fit object: a list with block_results (named list of per-sub-problem bayesomics_posterior objects), block_index (named list per Group, mapping block label -> block_results key), block_of_id (the resolved ID -> block assignment), blocks (block labels, in natural-sort order), and pooled.

Examples

data <- simu_db(nb_id = 12, nb_group = 2, nb_sample = 5)
ids <- unique(data$ID)
partition <- partition_by_id(stats::setNames(rep(c("A", "B"), length.out = length(ids)), ids))
fit <- fit_block_posterior(data, partition, kern = NULL, pooled = TRUE)
fit$blocks
#> [1] "A" "B"
